texts.preamble: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Smt. Sunita Goel on 3 August, 2016 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 211/05 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0706932005
texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused is stated to be the proprietor of M/s. Gupta Industries, where one Sh. Suresh Chand Gupta was the vendor, from where the food article, that is, 'Mustard Oil' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 05.03.2005, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) V.P.S. Chaudhary and Field Assistant (FA) Balwant Sah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. K.K. Sharma reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Gupta Indusrties at A-7, Milap Nagar, New Delhi-110059, where the vendor Sh. Suresh Chand Gupta was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of 'Mustard Oil' from the said vendor, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Smt. Sunita Goel on 3 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50761862/ 1 were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 31.03.2005, the PA found the sample to be misbranded being in violation of Rule 32 (e), (f) & (i) of PFA Rules. However, the Mustard Oil was found conforming to the standards. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. The investigation revealed that the vendor Sh. Suresh Chand Gupta was the first offender of Rule 32 and therefore, as per the policy of the department existing at that time, no prosecution was launched against him and only a warning was issued to him. It was also found that accused Sunita Goel was the sole proprietor of M/s. Gupta Industries to whom a previous warning had also been given for violation of Rule 32 by the LHA vide file no. SW/SDM/LHA/538/2003/PFA dated 21.09.2004. Since she was not the first offender for violation of Rule 32, she was not protected by the departmental policy. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was thus obtained from the Director PFA. The present complaint was filed in the court on 30.05.2009 against accused Sunita Goel alleging violation of section 2(ix)(k) as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for violation of Rule 32 (e), (f) and (i) of PFA Rules. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 30.09.2005. 4. Based on the PA report, notice of accusation under ection 251 CrPC was framed against the accused vide order dated 08.08.2006 for commission of the offence under section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act being in violation of Section 2(ix)(k) and Rule 32 (e), (f) and (i) of PFA Rules, to which she pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 FI V.P.S. Chaudhary, PW-2 FA Balwant Sah and PW-3 Sh. K.K. Sharma (the SDM / LHA) were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the steps undertaken by them for lifting the sample and also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, PA receipt Ex. PW-1/D and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received which opined the sample to be misbranded on the ground that the label was without declaration of batch number, date of manufacturing / packing and the best before date. Based on the report, investigation was carried out by PW-1 who wrote letter Ex. PW-1/G to the STO. It transpired that M/s. Gupta Industries was the proprietorship concern of accused Sunita Goel who had been given earlier warning Ex. PW-1/H. After completion of investigation, consent Ex. PW-1/I was obtained from the then Director, PFA and thereafter, complaint Ex. PW-1/J was filed in the court. Intimation letter Ex. PW-1/K along with copy of PA report were sent to the accused through post. During cross-examination, the witnesses denied that the accused was a household lady or that her husband used to run the business or that the samples were not taken properly or that no previous warning was issued to her or that the Mustard Oil was not for retail sale or that the sample was not ready for sale. They however accepted that accused was not present at the spot at the time of sampling. Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Smt. Sunita Goel on 3 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50761862/ 2 6. Subsequent to filing of an application under section 311 CrPC, the prosecution examined FSO Sh. D.V. Singh who produced the office file containing the warning letter Ex. PW-1/H issued previously to the accused Sunita Goel vide dispatch register Ex. PW-4/A. During cross- examination, he stated that he had sent the letter through registered post. 7. Statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.PC was recorded on 01.08.2013 and subsequently on 24.02.2015 wherein she expressed her ignorance about the sampling proceedings, stating that she was not present at the spot. She questioned the PA Report and stated that a distinguished parafix (sic: prefix) number "TF No. 002" was given on the bottles. She however did not lead any evidence in defence.
texts.arguments: 8. In these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the prosecution has been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused as she has not been able to rebut the findings of the PA report. It is submitted that even the accused has not denied the factum of misbranding, though has claimed that she had not received previous warning. Ld. SPP has argued that the stand of the accused fails because the previous warning and also the factum of its being sent to the accused have been duly established through PW-4. 9. On the other hand, ld. Defence counsel has argued that the prosecution has not been able to establish guilt of the accused. It is contented that the sample was not lifted properly. It is then submitted that the material on record is not sufficient to establish that any previous warning was ever issued or served upon the accused so as to deny her the benefit of departmental policy wherein a warning was only to be issued for first violation of Rule 32 instead of launching prosecution. In the judgment titled as S. S. Gokul Krishnan v. State [2009(1) FAC 132], it has been held that such policy bearing no.F6(228)/85/ENF./PFA dated 23.09.1985 was in operation and during this period and no prosecution could have been launched against a first time violator of Rule 32. 24. The judgement relied upon by the accused titled as Gapi Ram v. State of Haryana [1987 (1) PFA cases 153] would not be applicable to the present case as it is clear that the letter was sent to the accused at her complete and correct address. 25. The accused has also cited judgement titled as State v. Subhash Chand [2012(2) JCC 1004] to claim that no service can be said to have taken place in the absence of the AD card.
